summary: This paper resolves four fundamental open mathematical questions regarding quantum-state rugosity left open by Céleri and Soares-Pinto (2026): (1) measurement-induced resource convertibility via Blackwell dichotomies and polytope criteria; (2) exact trichotomy for inequality collapse, 2-copy superadditivity of measured relative entropy, and bipartite monotonicity/separable superadditivity; (3) BKM-variance tightened thermodynamic sensitivity bounds and unitary no-saturation dichotomies; and (4) pure-state necessity and uniformly tightened spectral-span quantum speed limits. The results are exceptionally supported by 20 constructive Lean 4 theorems, 16 exact rational SHA-256 certificates, and 67 adversarial test cases.
